claims.text: Real-time IR feedback can be used during SLM of CoCrFeMnNi to adapt laser power and scanning speed during each layer.
Adaptive adjustment of laser power and scanning speed will stabilize melt-pool dynamics.
Real-time feedback will produce a more uniform melt-pool geometry.
Real-time feedback will produce a more uniform melt-pool temperature distribution.
Immediate adjustments to laser power and scan speed will counteract melt-pool instabilities.
Stabilizing melt-pool behavior through adaptive control will reduce thermal gradients.
Stabilizing melt-pool behavior through adaptive control will reduce residual stresses.
Adaptive melt-pool control will promote more uniform solidification.
Adaptive melt-pool control will reduce keyhole porosity.
Adaptive melt-pool control will reduce incomplete-fusion defects.
Reduced thermal gradients, residual stresses, and fabrication defects will improve dimensional precision.
Reduced thermal gradients, residual stresses, and fabrication defects will improve mechanical properties.
Adaptive IR feedback will yield a more uniform microstructure than fixed-parameter SLM.
Adaptive IR feedback will yield lower porosity than fixed-parameter SLM.
Adaptive IR feedback will yield lower residual stress than fixed-parameter SLM.
Adaptive IR feedback will improve the dimensional accuracy of CoCrFeMnNi parts relative to fixed-parameter SLM.
Adaptive IR feedback will improve the mechanical integrity of CoCrFeMnNi parts relative to fixed-parameter SLM.
The intervention's benefits will be most pronounced within optimized energy-density ranges and in an inert-gas environment.
Environmental fluctuations, powder inconsistencies, or extreme build geometries may limit the intervention's effectiveness.
